subject: Capacity concordance request — dedicated GPU fleet sizing for Moonshot Labs
messages:
From: Sylvia Yang <sylvia@moonshot.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Chris Tan <chris.tan@mlinfra.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity planning — initial telemetry + asks

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're scoping a dedicated fleet with predictable latency for our conversational agent (customer support + account intelligence). Before we lock a budgeting window, the exec team asked for a concrete sizing recommendation from Redwood so we can compare runway/cost.

Quick summary of what we expect:
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~1,200 (estimated 09:00–11:00 PT and 16:00–18:00 PT)
- Average prompt length: 60 tokens; average response length: 220 tokens (long-tail to ~1,200 tokens on rare queries)
- Target p95 latency: <= 350ms for short flows (prompt+response under 600 tokens); p99 goal best-effort
- Model family: prefer Llama 2 13B or similar open model with quantization if it keeps quality within acceptable range
- Session affinity: yes — users keep session context, KV cache reuse expected for 60–120s between messages
- QoS requirements: 99.5% availability; burst tolerance for 3x baseline for 30 minutes

Attached a small sample of recent telemetry (anonymized) and a spreadsheet with the token distribution we could share. Can you send over a compact questionnaire we should fill that will let you size a dedicated pool and suggest GPU SKUs + oversubscription guidance? Also, is there a recommended rollout cadence (pilot -> canary -> full) you usually suggest for this size?

Appreciate it — looking to have an internal decision by next Friday.

Best,
Sylvia Yang
Head of Product
Moonshot Labs

Attachments: sample-telemetry-snippet.json
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Sylvia Yang <sylvia@moonshot.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — initial telemetry + asks

Hi Sylvia — great summary, and thanks for the telemetry.

I've attached our fleet_capacity_template.xlsx — it's intentionally short and focused on the inputs our sizing engine uses: concurrent sessions (by bucket), token distributions for prompt/response, session TTL, model family and acceptable quantization, expected p50/p95/p99 target latencies, and retention/SLA constraints. If you can populate the green fields we can run a preliminary sizing and recommend GPU SKUs + oversubscription ratios within 48 hours.

A couple of quick clarifying asks (helps accuracy):
- Are the 1,200 "concurrent sessions" measured as active sessions (generating output) or connected sessions (idle with cache)?
- For the rare long responses (~1,200 tokens), how frequent are they (1 in 500? 1 in 5k?), and do they generally appear in bursts?
- Do you need in-region (us-west) guarantees or multi-region active-active for failover?

Pilot cadence: we usually recommend a 3-stage rollout: pilot (1–2 GPUs equivalent capacity) to validate latency and correctness, canary at 10–20% of traffic with traffic shaping and fallback to hosted model, then full ramp with autoscale guardrails. For a 1,200 concurrent baseline, we typically size the canary to expose bottlenecks early (real user traffic at 10–15%).

I've looped in Marissa (solutions lead) and Ben (capacity architect) to help with workload-specific batching/quantization recommendations once you return the sheet.

Available times for a 30-min sizing call tomorrow: 11:00–12:00 PT or 15:00–16:00 PT. Does either work?

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Attachment: fleet_capacity_template.xlsx
From: Sylvia Yang <sylvia@moonshot.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Chris Tan <chris.tan@mlinfra.com>
Date: 2027-06-19T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — initial telemetry + asks

Aditya — thanks, the 11:00 PT slot works. Quick answers inline: 
- Concurrent sessions: 1,200 is active-generation (clients issuing prompts). Idle connections are tracked separately and not part of the 1,200 figure.
- Long responses: roughly 1 in 1,200 requests is >1,000 tokens; they tend to be non-bursty (rare reports).
- Region: start with us-west single-region for latency, but we want a documented plan for multi-region failover in the proposal.

I've completed the green fields in the spreadsheet and attached it back. Also attached a 30-second sample of our telemetry export that shows token-distribution and per-session inter-arrival times.

See you on the call.

—Sylvia

Attachments: fleet_capacity_template.xlsx (filled), sample-telemetry-snippet.json
